alalal-e17731-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 5: whether one must resist the power of the devil, and whether we should want to be tempted.

alalal-e17731-d1e113.summary: States the second question on this part: whether one must resist the power of the devil.

alalal-e17731-d1e120.summary: First objection: whoever resists power resists God's ordinance (Romans 13), so one should not resist the devil's power.

alalal-e17731-d1e130.summary: Second objection: Jeremiah urged submission to Nebuchadnezzar, who signifies the devil's power.

alalal-e17731-d1e143.summary: Third objection: one should bear what one has deserved by sin, and the devil's harassment is deserved by sin, as the Gloss on Psalm 105 says that human sins, not his own strength, made him powerful.

alalal-e17731-d1e168.summary: Fourth objection: Psalm 25:2 asks God to test and try us; temptation comes through the devil's power, so we should desire to be subject to it.

alalal-e17731-d1e184.summary: Sed contra: Matthew 6:13, 'and lead us not into temptation'.

alalal-e17731-d1e191.summary: Sed contra: 1 Peter 5:9, 'resist him, firm in faith'.

alalal-e17731-d1e198.summary: Solution: whether we should not want to be tempted was discussed earlier; here, the devil must be resisted with all one's strength, since 'devil' names a substance depraved in will, which uses its granted power only for evil ends.
claims: The devil and his power must be resisted with all one's strength, since he uses power only for evil ends.

alalal-e17731-d1e219.summary: Reply to the first objection: all power is ordained by God, but sometimes the wicked will of the one in power is joined to it, and in that respect one must resist; if power remained only in the divine order, punishing evildoers and praising the good, it should not be resisted at all.
claims: One resists not the God-ordained power itself but the wicked will joined to it.

alalal-e17731-d1e241.summary: Reply to the second: Jeremiah counselled submission to bodily captivity, not to spiritual captivity through sin, which comes from wicked intention, not from the order of power.

alalal-e17731-d1e257.summary: Reply to the third: that holds for bodily afflictions, as with Job, but one must never consent to the sin the devil intends, as Job did not sin with his lips.
claims: Bodily afflictions from the devil may be borne, but never consent to sin.

alalal-e17731-d1e273.summary: On whether we should want to be tempted: no, because temptation involves the devil's perverse will, which is to be resisted, and because of our weakness, which should avoid occasions of falling. David in Psalm 25 desired temptation's effect, purity, not the trial itself, asking to be so confirmed by God's power that temptation could lead only to purity, as Augustine prays 'give what you command' and a desert father prayed for strength to bear temptations rather than their absence.
claims: We should not want to be tempted, because of the devil's perverse will and our own weakness.
One may desire the purifying effect of temptation and strength to bear it.

alalal-e17731.summary: Article 5 asks whether the devil's power must be resisted and whether we should want to be tempted. Objections cite the duty not to resist God-ordained power, Jeremiah's counsel to serve Nebuchadnezzar, the justice of bearing deserved punishment, and the psalmist's prayer to be tried. Albert holds that the devil must be resisted with all one's strength, since his will is depraved and he uses power only for evil. Power as ordained by God is not to be resisted, but the wicked will joined to it is. Bodily afflictions may be borne, as by Job, but there must be no consent to sin. We should not want to be tempted, both because temptation carries the devil's perverse intent and because of our weakness. David desired only temptation's purifying effect and the strength to bear it.
claims: The devil must be resisted with all one's strength.
One resists not God-ordained power as such but the wicked will joined to it.
We should not wish to be tempted, though we may desire temptation's purifying effect and strength to bear it.
